extracted.intended_audience: university/institutional public information officers, research communications staff, and researchers preparing press releases about NIH-funded research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for institutions preparing and coordinating press releases or other public communications about research supported by NIH, including when and how to notify and work with NIH communications offices, attribution/funding language, embargo coordination, and distribution channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with NIH communications offices
rubrics_metrics.description: We may both be planning to issue news releases on the same work. For this reason, it's very important that we coordinate our activities and distribution plans so that we maximize our efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the relevant NIH institute or center communications office early; NIH communications staff will work closely with you to determine the best way to promote the research and to decide who should take the lead if more than one NIH unit funded the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify NIH when a paper is accepted or when you are writing about NIH-funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: When you learn that an NIH-funded scientist at your institution has a paper accepted for publication, please let us know. If the paper will soon be published, we'd still like to hear from you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to issuing a press release concerning the outcome of this research, please notify us so NIH communications offices can consider issuing or coordinating a release and identify other promotion opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a quote from an NIH official
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are preparing a press release about NIH-funded research, consider including a quote from an expert at the NIH institute funding the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such comments offer outside perspective on the significance of the finding and the value of supporting such research. If you'd like a quote, contact NIH communications staff to request one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge NIH funding in releases and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication, press release, or other document about research supported by an NIH award must include an acknowledgment of NIH award support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the required language format, e.g.: “Research reported in this publication was supported by the National Institute of General Medical Sciences of the National Institutes of Health under award number R01GM085232.” Mention NIH early in the text when possible; grant numbers and full award information may be placed in the footer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include an active link to NIH (https://www.nih.gov) in releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a funding acknowledgement and an active link to https://www.nih.gov in your news releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An active link to NIH helps demonstrate the link between taxpayer dollars and research advances; include it early in the release or in a prominent place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow and coordinate embargo policies
rubrics_metrics.description: We follow the same embargo policies that you do and won't do anything to jeopardize paper publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify NIH of publication timing and embargoes so NIH can coordinate distribution under embargo. If NIH cannot meet your deadlines, they will notify you immediately so you can proceed independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider issuing or tailoring a joint NIH release
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuing a joint release. If you do not plan to issue a separate release, you might consider tailoring ours for your local reporters or press contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH releases undergo extensive review for scientific accuracy and editing and may serve as excellent background for preparing local materials. Discuss tailoring and timing with NIH communications staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use alternative promotion options (informal notes, web summaries, media availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Options can include: an informal note to reporters who you may not reach with your release, posting a brief summary on the NIH institute's web site, or highlighting your release or the work in the institute's publications; a short 'media availability' announcement informing reporters about the latest work and that an NIH expert is available for further comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with NIH to pick the most appropriate combination of outreach tools depending on timing, audience, and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange interviews with NIH experts as secondary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH can arrange interviews with NIH experts as secondary sources for reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH communications staff can put you in contact with NIH experts and disease specialists, particularly in areas that are new or unfamiliar, to provide additional comment or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge your institution in NIH releases and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH can acknowledge your institution in NIH releases and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you coordinate with NIH communications staff, they may include institutional acknowledgment when NIH highlights the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH to enhance news distribution and reach different audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH can enhance your news distribution by reaching different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH posts all news releases to its News & Events page and sends them to a subscribing listserv of reporters, advocacy groups, scientific organizations, NIH constituents, and members of the public; individual institutes also conduct unique outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include links to your material on appropriate NIH websites
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH communications offices may include links to your material on appropriate NIH websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the relevant institute/center communications office to request linkage or spotting of your material on NIH pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight researcher advances on NIH channels
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH can highlight your researchers’ advances on our web site, in Congressional material and other publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with NIH to determine if and how NIH might feature the work in broader NIH communications products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with NIH to identify researchers doing exciting/innovative work
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH communications staff can help identify researchers at your institutions who are doing exciting and innovative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be useful for cross-promotion, expert identification, or linking related content across NIH and institutional channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help make research understood by many audiences and explain taxpayer link
rubrics_metrics.description: Help us explain to your readers and the public the link between taxpayer dollars and research advances at your institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate with NIH to craft language and materials that communicate significance to lay and specialized audiences, including messaging about the role of federal funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine lead NIH institute/center when multiple NIH units funded the work
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one NIH institute or center funded the work, we will determine who at NIH should take the lead on our activities and be your main contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform NIH of all funding sources so NIH can identify an appropriate lead communications contact and coordinate internal review and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH distribution channels and contact institute/center PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: All NIH news releases are posted to our News & Events page and sent to a self-subscribing listserv. Individual NIH institutes and centers post releases on their respective news sites and conduct media outreach unique to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the most relevant institutes and centers to collaborate; contact NIH to locate institute and center PIOs. Consider subscribing to NIH listservs for distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EurekAlert! and mark NIH as the funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH's main source for distributing news releases under embargo is EurekAlert!. NIH's EurekAlert! Web site features NIH news releases, as well as NIH-funded news releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If posting to EurekAlert!, be sure to click NIH as a funding source so it will appear on the NIH EurekAlert! web site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide and obtain contact information for NIH PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact information for NIH PIOs to quickly facilitate communication and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please contact NIH to locate institute and center PIOs; NIH communications staff (e.g., Craig Fritz) can assist with press-release coordination across NIH's 27 institutes and centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct reporters to NIH for additional comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Send reporters to us for additional comments on your researcher’s work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reporters need secondary-source comments or additional context, direct them to NIH communications staff and experts to avoid misinterpretation and provide authoritative perspective.
